thread.title: Apple Earnings: Not Spectacular, But Will Still Drive Stock To $200

author: Martin Tillier
title: Apple Earnings: Not Spectacular, But Will Still Drive Stock To $200
text:
Apple (Shutterstock photo)
A week or so ago, the internet was awash with stories like this , stating with certainty that when Apple ( AAPL ) released their earnings for the first quarter of 2018, iPhone X sales would be disappointing.
One analyst even went so far as to declare the X “dead.”
When the release came after the market close yesterday, what we got was something quite different. In the words of CEO Tim Cook, the first quarter numbers showed that "customers chose iPhone X more than any other iPhone each week in the March quarter, just as they did following its launch in the December quarter."
The obituary, it seems, was somewhat premature.
Looking through those earnings though, what becomes clear is that those alarmist pieces were not only mistaken as to the sales figures themselves, but also in their assumption that Apple’s overall fate was inextricably tied with that of their high-end phone.
Overall, iPhone sales were okay, if not spectacular, coming in at around the expected number. However, the details in this report suggest that even if reports of slow sales of the X turn out to be ill-timed rather than just flat out wrong, Apple will continue to thrive, and the stock will hit new highs.
That is because the real news here came on two fronts where massive growth is possible going forward.
Firstly, Apple’s services division, which consists of revenue from apps, subscriptions and the like, is beginning to fulfill its massive potential. Revenue in that segment grew a massive 31% year over year to exceed $9 billion. That represents a significant and growing percentage of the company’s overall revenue of $61.1 billion, and that is no accident.
As some have fretted over possible saturation of the smartphone market in general, and of iPhones in particular, Tim Cook and the management team at Apple have been preparing for that possibility, by expanding potential revenue streams. They are not the only company to realize that once consumers buy into an ecosystem there are many ways to take their money (see Amazon AMZN and Google GOOGL ), but they have been very successful in making that happen.
Amazon, Google, Microsoft ( MSFT ) and others are competing for that revenue and there could yet be a shift in market share that works against them, but for now Apple is sitting pretty.
That is especially true in the other area of positive news to come out of this earnings report, regarding China. It doesn’t take a genius to realize that the largest market in the world is a good place to show growth, and Apple did just that last quarter. Overall business in China grew by twenty one percent.
Logically that means that the iPhone must have done well there, and Cook said on the earnings call that the iPhone X was the biggest selling iPhone in China last quarter. Obviously, given the population of the country, that is a positive, but when you combine that with the “ecosystem growth” tactics outlined above it has the potential to fuel further growth for a long time to come.
AAPL, the stock, as you might have expected, responded positively to the report. Part of the jump is no doubt attributable to the announcement of a massive, $100 billion return of capital to shareholders through buybacks. To some that will no doubt prove their point that giving tax cuts to already cash-rich corporations doesn’t prompt them to invest heavily, but rather to just further enrich Wall Street, but bear in mind that Apple generates over $50 billion of free cash flow every year.
If they want to invest as well as buy back shares, they are quite capable of doing so. For now, though, growth by acquisition isn’t needed, so returning at least of the gigantic pile of cash to shareholders is the right thing to do.
Following earnings, there are therefore a lot of reasons to be positive about AAPL, but the most important is the most basic. Despite consistently proving the legion of doubters wrong, AAPL is still priced as if the end is nigh, with both forward and trailing P/E’s lagging the market average significantly. The real glory days of spectacular growth driven by handset sales may be behind us, but Apple is driving growth in other ways and as that sinks in, AAPL can be expected to blow past the previous highs and march on up to $200.
